search_providers.description: Find local businesses that can do a job. Searches Darwin's agent index first; when no agent covers it (status no_match), returns phone-only and text-enabled local businesses Platypus can book. Each result carries routing signals (typical price, median reply time, acceptance) and next_step. Booking statuses: pending (asked, waiting on the owner), countered (owner proposed another time or price), confirmed (the owner said yes on the call or by text; only then is it booked), declined, expired, cancelled, rescheduled, completed, no_show, disputed.

service.description: What the customer needs, e.g. 'oil change'

window.description: A time range the customer can make, e.g. tomorrow 12:00 to 17:00 local time, as ISO-8601

channel_state.description: phone_only: we will call. text_enabled: the owner opted in to texts

next_step.description: What request_booking would do for this provider right now

get_availability.description: Known open slots for a business within a window. Empty does not mean unavailable: Platypus asks the owner when it does not know.

window.description: A time range the customer can make, e.g. tomorrow 12:00 to 17:00 local time, as ISO-8601

request_booking.description: Ask a business for a booking. Returns immediately with status pending and the route Platypus chose: darwin_act (an existing agent), call (an AI voice call that discloses itself first), or text (the owner opted in). Results are asynchronous: the owner answers on a phone call or by text, usually within minutes. Poll get_booking with the booking_id every few seconds until the status is no longer pending. Never tell the user a booking is confirmed until get_booking says confirmed. Booking statuses: pending (asked, waiting on the owner), countered (owner proposed another time or price), confirmed (the owner said yes on the call or by text; only then is it booked), declined, expired, cancelled, rescheduled, completed, no_show, disputed.
